With the consent of the parties, the matter is heard finally.

5. This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act of 1988') has been filed by the claimants / appellants aggrieved by award dated 21/09/2016 passed on 21/09/2016 in claim case No.132/2015 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bemetara, District- Bemetara (CG).

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bemetara, District- Bemetara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
6. Facts of the case in brief is that the claimants/appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the Act of 1988 claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.46,50,896/- on account of death of the deceased - Rakesh Sonit in an accident which took place on 29/10/2011 on national highway,
Chowki- Maro, Police Station - Nandghat due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing CG-07-E-6012 driven by respondent No.1 / driver owned by respondents no.2 and 3 and insured by respondent No.4 / insurance company.
The said accident was reported to the police station - Nandghat and offence under Section 304-A of IPC was registered and after due investigation, charge sheet was filed before the competent Court.

It was pleaded in the claim application that the deceased - Rakesh Sonit was aged about 30 years and was working as Panchayat Karmi, Grade - III in the Government Primary School, Lalpur, Sankul - Maro, Development Block - Nawagarh and was earning Rs.19,034/- per month.
The appellants / claimants were dependent upon the salary of the deceased.
7. The claim application was resisted by respondents 1, 2 and 3 and filed their joint written statement and accepted the admitted averments and denied the averments of the claim application.
They denied happening of the accident by the offending vehicle and pleaded that the compensation claimed is excessive.
Respondent No.1/driver had valid and effective driving license and the offending vehicle is having fitness, permit and insured with respondent No.4/Insurance Company.
Therefore, if any compensation is awarded, liability to pay the same would be upon respondent No.4 / insurance company.
8. Respondent No.4/ insurance company also filed its written statement and denied the averments of the claim application.
It also denied happening of Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23082 the incident and denied the profession and income of the deceased.
It was pleaded that on the date of incident, the deceased was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the motor cycle.

There is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy as the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective permit / fitness and driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license.

Therefore, it was prayed that the claim application may be Smt. Khemwati Sonit vs Fiirtoo Ram Dewangan on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47409673/
2 rejected against it.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Learned Tribunal framed as many as 4 issues.
The issue with regard to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1 / driver thereby causing death of Rakesh Sonit, has been decided in favour of the appellants/claimants.
The issue with regard to violation of the insurance policy has also been decided against respondent no.4.
Issue no.3 was relief and cost, a compensation of Rs.13,17,000/- was awarded in favour of the appellants / claimants.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants argued that though the learned Tribunal has accepted the income of the deceased, however, deducted  amount for contributory negligence which is absolutely perverse and liable to be set aside.
He further submits that the deceased was in regular employment and therefore, the learned Tribunal ought to have granted future prospects to the claimant / appellants.
He further submits that the compensation awarded on other non-pecuniary heads are also on the lower side which requires suitable enhancement.

To buttress his submission, learned counsel places reliance upon decision of the Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and ors., (2018) 18 SCC 130 and judgment of this Court in the case of Narsingh Bareth v. Parvati Devi and ors, 2020 SCC OnLine Chh 1000.

sentences.text: 11. Learned counsel for respondent No.4 supported the award passed by the learned Tribunal and submitted that deduction of half as done by the learned Tribunal is on account of contributory negligence as from the statement of the wife of the deceased, it is evident that the deceased was not holding any driving license.
He prays that the appeal may be dismissed.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23082 13.

Firstly, it has to be seen that whether the learned Tribunal was justified in deducting 50% ()
amount of compensation as the deceased was not holding valid and effective driving license.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sudhir Kumar Rana v. Surinder Singh and ors. reported in (2008)
12 SCC 436 in paragraph 9 held as under - "9.

entities.text:
Sudhir Kumar Rana v. Surinder Singh and ors. reported in (2008)
12 SCC 436
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.
The same, by itself, in our opinion, may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini-truck which was being driven rashly and negligently.
It is one thing to say that the appellant was not possessing any licence but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two-wheeler rashly and negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having a licence, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence."
14.

Further in the case of Dinesh Kumar J. @ Dinesh J. v. National Insurance Company Limited and ors. reported in (2018) 1 SCC 750 Hon'ble Supreme Court has also referred the judgment of Sudhir Smt. Khemwati Sonit vs Fiirtoo Ram Dewangan on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47409673/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Kumar (supra) with approval and finding of contributory negligence on this count was set aside.

15. In light of the above authoritative pronouncement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and on examination of the records of the case, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the learned Tribunal fell in error in deducting 50% amount of compensation as the deceased was not holding valid and effective driving license.
The driver of the offending vehicle was prosecuted for an offence punishable under Section 304 (A) of IPC.
There is no clinching evidence to show that the deceased in any manner contributed to the accident.
Simply because he was not holding any valid and effective driving license would not ipso facto mean to have contributed to the accident.
The income of the deceased is proved by cogent and prudent evidence.

16. Taking guidance from the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009) 6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi and ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra), this Court hereby computes the compensation in the following manner - Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23082 1

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the appeal till its realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally held liable to pay the compensation.
18. After the enhanced compensation is deposited, Rs.7,00,000/- each shall be invested in the name of appellant No.2 and 3 as fixed deposit in a nationalised bank till they attain majority.
Rs.10,00,000/- shall be invested in the name of appellant No.1 as fixed deposit in a nationalised bank for a period of 5 years.
She will be entitled to receive the interest accrued on it.
Rest of the amount deposited shall be paid to appellant No.1 by Bank Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23082 transaction / account payee cheque.
19. The appeal thus allowed in part as indicated above.
